title: 卜算子·咏梅
englishTitle: Song of Divination: Ode to the Plum Blossom
author: Lu You

translation: Beyond the post station, by the broken bridge
It blooms in loneliness, owned by no one
Wind and rain add to its burden
It has no wish to compete for spring
Let the other flowers envy as they will
Fallen, ground into mud and dust

annotations.驿外: beyond the post station — a remote, deserted place
annotations.无主: without an owner — blooming for no one
annotations.更著: and furthermore adds — piling on hardship
annotations.争春: compete for spring — rival other flowers

appreciation: The plum blossom blooms in winter, so poets use it as a symbol of integrity under pressure. Lu You, repeatedly sidelined in his political career, saw himself in this lonely flower by a broken bridge: crushed into mud, yet its fragrance — its character — never changes. Chairman Mao later wrote a famous reply poem with the opposite spirit.
